text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A Turkish prosecutor demands the lifting of immunity from prosecution of two government MPs, Sedat Bucak and Mehmet Agar, linked to a security scandal.
- A parliamentary commission draft report on alleged ties between the state and underworld identifies links between officials and organised crime.
- A document is found proving that mobile phones in Turkey are bugged, after denials by the interior and transport ministers that such bugging occurred.
- The Israeli intelligence service warns Turkey that Syria is sheltering Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels as a card against Turkey.
- Two programme producers from Cevre Radio are sentenced to 20 months imprisonment for interviewing families of 11 people killed in an attack on a minibus in the southeast last year.
- Turkey achieved the second largest rise in tourist numbers among European countries in 1996 according to research by the publication International Tourism Overview.
- The number of tourists visiting Turkey in February decreased 3.2 percent from a year earlier.
- A French criminology institute report highlights the involvement of Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels in drug trafficking.
